problem: LLMs and 2D VLMs are not grounded in the 3D physical world (spatial relations, affordances, layout), and 3D-language data and pretrained 3D-language encoders are scarce, so no general 3D-based LLM exists.
motivation: Holistic 3D scene representations give LLMs long-term scene memory and let them reason about spatial relations and affordances beyond what 2D or text-only inputs allow. Because no large 3D-language corpus or 3D-CLIP-style encoder exists, the authors generate data with ChatGPT and lift 2D features into 3D so pretrained 2D VLMs can be reused.
key_idea: Build language-aligned 3D features from rendered multi-view 2D features, feed them into a pretrained 2D VLM (BLIP-2 / Flamingo) with 3D position embeddings and location tokens, and train it on 300k GPT-generated 3D-language samples.
insight: Lifting 2D CLIP-space features into 3D lets frozen-encoder 2D VLMs be reused without training a 3D encoder. 3D-LLM beats single-image and multi-view-image VLM baselines on ScanQA, 3DMV-VQA and held-in tasks, which suggests that organized 3D structure matters and that unordered multi-view features lose 3D information. Removing the Flamingo perceiver gives only small drops (BLEU-1 29.2 vs 30.3, CIDEr 58.9 vs 59.2). There is no ablation of the localization mechanism.
method: 3D-language data generation: three ChatGPT prompting schemes (boxes-demonstration-instruction with room/object AABBs and 0-3 few-shot demos, ChatCaptioner with BLIP-2 answering, and revision-based transfer between data types) yield over 300k samples from Objaverse, ScanNet and HM3D/HM3DSem.

3D feature extractor: render multi-view images, extract pixel-aligned dense 2D features (ConceptFusion-style), lift to N x D_v point features via direct reconstruction, gradslam feature fusion, or a neural voxel field (3D-CLR).

2D VLM backbones: the point features go through the Perceiver / Q-Former of Flamingo-9B, BLIP-2 ViT-g OPT-2.7B or BLIP-2 ViT-g FlanT5-XL. For BLIP-2 the Q-Former is fine-tuned and the LLM kept frozen; for Flamingo the perceiver, gated cross-attention and location-token embeddings are trained.
3D position embeddings: sin/cos embeddings for x, y, z (each D_v/3) concatenated to the 3D features.
Location tokens: AABB corners discretized into voxel-integer tokens added to the LLM vocabulary, with input and output embeddings of these tokens unfrozen, so grounding is done by generating tokens.

Object navigation formulation: an online partial 3D feature, current position and history are fed to the 3D-LLM, which predicts a 3D waypoint or stop, executed by an off-the-shelf DD-PPO local policy.

setting.backbone: BLIP-2 (ViT-g + OPT-2.7B or FlanT5-XL) and Flamingo-9B, 2D VLMs fine-tuned with 3D inputs
setting.model_size: Flamingo 9B; BLIP-2 ViT-g with OPT-2.7B / FlanT5-XL
setting.training_data: 300k+ ChatGPT-generated 3D-language samples (Objaverse, ScanNet, HM3D), split 8:1:1; then fine-tuned on ScanQA / 3DMV-VQA / ScanRefer
setting.observation: 3D point cloud with lifted CLIP features built from rendered multi-view RGB(-D) images; online partial 3D features for navigation
setting.action_space: navigation: LLM-predicted 3D waypoints plus stop, executed by a DD-PPO local policy with low-level actions
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D) for the navigation demo; otherwise static ScanNet/HM3D/Objaverse scenes
setting.privileged: GT bounding boxes/semantics used for data generation; rendered RGB-D with GT camera poses for direct reconstruction; none stated for navigation

numbers_note: Object navigation is only shown as a qualitative episode on HM3D in the appendix; no navigation metrics were reported. Reported results are ScanQA, 3DMV-VQA, ScanRefer and held-in captioning/dialog, none of which are navigation benchmarks.
results: On ScanQA val, 3D-LLM (BLIP2-flant5) reaches BLEU-1 39.3 and CIDEr 69.4 versus ScanQA's 30.2 and 64.9. On the ScanQA test set it gets BLEU-1 38.3 and CIDEr 69.6, and it also beats 2D VLM baselines on held-in captioning, dialog and task decomposition. On 3DMV-VQA it reaches 58.6 overall, above 3D-CLR's 57.7.
limitations: Depends on rendering multi-view images of every scene to build features, which adds an extra rendering step.
Navigation is only shown qualitatively, with no quantitative navigation evaluation.
Grounding on ScanRefer is weaker than the dedicated ScanRefer model (ACC@0.25 30.3 vs 41.2), and EM on ScanQA is below ScanQA's.
